audit:S2-peripheral-irreducible.summary:
Step 2 is mathematically correct. I found no gap in the topology, only citation slips and a few routine steps that the text compresses.

What checks out:
- V is a solid torus with meridian lambda. For any slope mu meeting lambda once, R's lambda- and mu-closures are the 2-component unlink and the unknot, with covers S^1xS^2 and S^3. Choosing mu different from both probes is always possible (and not actually needed).
- Sikora's Theorem 21 assumes T1 and T2 are unequal unframed rational tangles, which matches the proof's hypothesis. It gives [X]=[R], so every closure of X has the same bracket as the matching closure of R. Using Sikora's normalization (unknot = 1, so delta vanishes at A=e^{i pi/4} only through extra circles), X's lambda- and mu-closures have determinants 0 and 1.
- Stoimenow Prop 6.5 says det is odd exactly for knots, so the mu-closure is a knot and X has no loops.
- |H_1(Sigma_2(L))| = det(L), with det 0 exactly when H_1 is infinite, so Y = M(mu) is an integral homology sphere. Then H_1(M)=Z and H_2(M)=0 (Mayer-Vietoris checked). lambda, the unique slope whose filling has infinite H_1, is K's preferred longitude, and mu is K's meridian.
- Each probe other than lambda gives an actual lens-space filling, possibly S^3.

Irreducibility is valid:
- b_1(M_0) >= 1 and H_1(M)=Z force every closed summand to have H_1=0, so each is a homology sphere. This also rules out an S^1xS^2 summand; H_2(M)=0 rules out a nonseparating sphere a second way.
- Lens spaces and S^3 are prime (S^3 by Alexander's theorem). So a homology-sphere summand of a lens-space filling must be S^3. If M_0(alpha) were S^3, the closed part would be the lens space, which homology forbids unless p=+-1, and then Alexander's theorem settles it.
- The Poincare conjecture is not needed.
- A local knot J in X makes Sigma_2(J) a closed summand of M, so it is excluded here. Concluding that the arc itself is unknotted uses Lickorish's criterion [BM, Theorem 3.5(1)], which contains Waldhausen's Z/2 Smith theorem.

sources_checked.source: A. Stoimenow, Square numbers, spanning trees and invariants of achiral knots, Comm. Anal. Geom. 13(3) (2005) 591-631
sources_checked.statement_paraphrase: The proposition says det(L) is odd if and only if L is a knot. Its proof notes that the Alexander polynomial of an n-component link is divisible by (t^{1/2}-t^{-1/2})^{n-1}, so 2^{n-1} divides det(L).
sources_checked.note: The 2^(c-1) divisibility is in the proof, not the statement. The statement alone ('det odd iff knot') is exactly what Step 2 uses for 'det 1 implies knot'.

sources_checked.source: O. Dasbach, D. Futer, E. Kalfagianni, X.-S. Lin, N. Stoltzfus, Alternating sum formulae for the determinant and other link invariants, J. Knot Theory Ramifications 19(6) (2010) 765-782 (preprint PDF at the cited URL)
sources_checked.location: Section 3 ('Dessins Determine the Determinant'), opening paragraph before Definition 3.1
sources_checked.statement_paraphrase: A passing remark: the determinant is |Alexander(-1)| = |Jones(-1)|, and it is the order of H_1 of the double branched cover. The text loosely says 'of the link complement'. There is no proof and no theorem number.
sources_checked.note: Supports only the finite-order clause, and informally. The clause 'det 0 iff H_1 infinite' is not in the source. It is standard (H_1 of the double branched cover has a square presentation matrix V+V^T or a Goeritz matrix of determinant +-det).

sources_checked.statement_paraphrase: System (1) is N(X+T_i)=L_i with T1 != T2 rational. Conjecture 2: a rational solution of a framed system is unique among all solutions. In Section 4, framed tangles are embeddings of two bands J1xI and J2xI (so no loops) and are taken up to balanced isotopy, where the location of framing twists does not matter. Section 4.1 requires T1 and T2 to be unequal as unframed tangles.
sources_checked.note: The proof's 'distinct underlying unframed slopes' matches 4.1. Balanced isotopy implies an ambient isotopy of the unframed, unoriented links, so double branched covers are homeomorphic (preserving orientation), which is all Step 2 needs.

sources_checked.location: Section 5 (bracket normalization); Section 8, Theorem 21 and proof; Corollary 19
sources_checked.statement_paraphrase: The bracket is normalized so the trivially framed unknot is 1, with each extra circle giving delta. Theorem 21: in any framed system (1), the bracket vector of a solution is uniquely determined. The proof expresses the two closure brackets through a 2x2 matrix whose determinant is (delta^2-1) times det([T_i]_0,[T_i]_inf). That determinant is nonzero because distinct rational tangles have distinct q-rationals (Corollary 19).
sources_checked.note: I re-derived det B myself. This gives [X]=[R], hence equal brackets, and so equal determinants, for the lambda- and mu-closures of X and R.

sources_checked.source: D. Buck and M. Mauricio, arXiv:1007.0948 (citing Lickorish, Prime knots and tangles, Trans. AMS 267 (1981))
sources_checked.statement_paraphrase: Tangles here have exactly two arcs. A tangle is locally knotted iff its double branched cover is non-prime with torus boundary. It is rational iff the cover is a solid torus. It is prime iff the cover is irreducible and boundary-irreducible.
sources_checked.note: Checked only for the local-knot question. Once Step 2 rules out loops, X fits Definition 3.1, and the irreducibility from Step 2 plus 3.5(1) excludes local knots.

sources_checked.location: Kneser-Milnor prime decomposition; Alexander's theorem; irreducibility of lens spaces; half-lives-half-dies; Mayer-Vietoris and Alexander duality for knot exteriors; lifting isotopies to double branched covers
sources_checked.statement_paraphrase: Every compact orientable 3-manifold has a unique prime decomposition. Every 2-sphere in S^3 bounds balls, so S^3 is prime. L(p,q) with p>=2 is prime. A manifold with torus boundary has b_1>=1. A knot exterior in an integral homology sphere has H_1=Z, H_2=0, and the longitude is its only filling slope with infinite H_1. Homeomorphisms of link pairs lift to the double branched covers.
sources_checked.note: Primality of L(p,q) needs no Poincare conjecture. Lift a homotopy-sphere summand to the universal cover S^3 and apply Alexander's theorem.

sources_checked.source: W. B. R. Lickorish, An Introduction to Knot Theory (GTM 175), Chapter 9 'Cyclic Branched Covers and the Goeritz Matrix'
sources_checked.location: Chapter 9 (chapter title confirmed by web search; theorem numbers not verified)
sources_checked.statement_paraphrase: A textbook treatment of presenting H_1 of the double branched cover by a symmetrized Seifert or Goeritz matrix, giving order |det| when det is nonzero and infinite H_1 when det is zero.
sources_checked.note: Suggested as a replacement for the [D] citation. The book itself was not opened.

findings.claim: "a link with c components has determinant divisible by 2^(c-1) [St, Proposition 6.5]"
findings.why: Stoimenow's Proposition 6.5 states only that det(L) is odd iff L is a knot. The 2^(c-1) divisibility appears inside its proof, via Torres/Hosokawa divisibility of the Alexander polynomial. The mathematics is right, and the proposition as stated is exactly what is needed (det 1 is odd, so the closure is a knot). The citation points to the proof rather than the statement.
findings.suggested_fix: Write: 'det 1 is odd, so the closure is a knot [St, Prop. 6.5: det(L) is odd iff L is a knot]'. Add the bibliographic data Comm. Anal. Geom. 13(3) (2005) 591-631.

findings.claim: "The order of first homology of a double branched cover is the determinant, with determinant zero indicating infinite first homology [D, Section 3]."
findings.why: DFKLS Section 3 contains only an unproved remark that the determinant is the order of H_1 of the double branched cover, loosely worded as 'of the link complement'. It says nothing about the det = 0 case, and Step 2 needs that case to identify lambda. The fact is true and standard, but the cited source does not establish the clause Step 2 relies on. The reference also omits its journal data.
findings.suggested_fix: Cite a textbook proof: H_1(Sigma_2(L)) has the square presentation matrix V+V^T (or a Goeritz matrix) with |determinant| = det(L), so it is finite of order det(L) iff det(L) != 0. For example, Lickorish, An Introduction to Knot Theory, Ch. 9. If [D] is kept, add J. Knot Theory Ramifications 19(6) (2010) 765-782.

findings.claim: "Prime decomposition of an actual lens-space filling forces each closed homology-sphere summand to be S^3. Hence no nontrivial sphere decomposition of M remains."
findings.why:
The conclusion is correct, but four routine inputs are not stated:
(a) L(p,q) with p>=2 is prime, and S^3 is prime (Alexander's theorem). Homology alone cannot see a summand like the Poincare sphere, so primality is genuinely needed.
(b) A case split. From L = M_0(alpha) # N with N a homology sphere, primality gives either M_0(alpha) = S^3 or N = S^3. The first case makes N = L, which homology forbids unless p=+-1; then L = S^3 and N = S^3 by Alexander.
(c) M_0(alpha) may be reducible, so the argument should use primality of L, not a naive matching of prime factors.
(d) A prime manifold with torus boundary is irreducible.
None of this needs the Poincare conjecture.
findings.suggested_fix: Insert two sentences. 'If M = M' # N with N closed, then H_1(N)=0 and L = M'(alpha) # N. Since lens spaces and S^3 are prime [Kneser-Milnor; Alexander; lens spaces are irreducible], either N = S^3, or M'(alpha) = S^3 and N = L, which forces |H_1(L)|=1 and hence N = S^3. Thus every sphere in M bounds a ball. A prime manifold with torus boundary is irreducible.'

findings.claim: Exclusion of a local knot in a string of X, implicit in "This also implies that M is irreducible ... Hence no nontrivial sphere decomposition of M remains."
findings.why: A local knot J contributes the closed summand Sigma_2(J). H_1(M)=Z forces det(J)=1, and the lens-space argument forces Sigma_2(J) = S^3. So the step correctly kills any local knot whose double branched cover is nontrivial. Concluding that the arc is actually unknotted needs Waldhausen's Z/2 Smith theorem. That theorem is packaged inside Lickorish's criterion [BM, Thm 3.5(1),(2)], but the proof never makes this connection; it is only implicit in Step 5.
findings.suggested_fix: After proving irreducibility, add: 'By [BM, Theorem 3.5(1)] (Lickorish), X is therefore not locally knotted.'

findings.claim: "X an arbitrary framed 2-tangle" together with "Thus X has no closed components ..."
findings.why: In Sikora's framed setting (Section 4), framed tangles are by definition two bands J1xI and J2xI, so loops are already excluded. The determinant argument matters only under the broader Section 2.1 reading, where tangles may have loops. It is valid there, and it is also what places X within BM Definition 3.1 (exactly two arcs), which Step 5 needs. This is a presentation point, not a gap.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one sentence: Sikora's framed tangles have no loops by definition, and the argument shows the result also holds if loops are allowed, which is needed to apply [BM, Def. 3.1/Thm. 3.5].

audit:S4-longitude-case.summary:
The mathematics of Step 4 is correct. I found no gap. I checked it against the arXiv:1508.05900v2 PDF (pdftotext copy at /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-calebbarnett/7610ac96-4d03-4d32-b526-8a5647837809/scratchpad/rr/rr.txt).

(1) Prop 7.8 (p. 45) covers a knot in Z#(S^1xS^2) with an L-space surgery and concludes that its complement is a generalized solid torus (GST). Here Z = S^3. The knot K' is the core of the lambda-filling, and the other probe gives a lens-space filling (S^3 at distance one), so the hypotheses hold exactly.

(2) Def 7.2 (p. 43) defines a GST as a Floer simple Y with deg of Delta-bar(Y) < g_Y. The overline is present, and Delta-bar = (1-t)*tau-bar (p. 6). So the proof's "Floer simple and deg bar-Delta < g_M" is exactly the definition.

(3) g_Y (Section 7 preamble, p. 42) is the positive generator of the image of boundary homology in H_1/T. RR print this as "im phi", an evident misprint. RR list as equivalent: the minimal number of boundary components of a surface generating H_2(Y, boundary), and the order of the homological longitude in H_1(Y). They also note |T| = k_Y*g_Y. With H_1(M) = Z, every reading gives g_M = 1 (and k_M = 1). So deg bar-Delta(M) = 0; Cor 7.4 and the torsion formula in the proof of 7.8 even give bar-Delta(M) ~ 1.

(4) The first clause of Cor 2.3 (p. 7) needs only boundary-incompressible plus Floer simple, and gives ||Y|| = deg bar-Delta - 1. In the counterfactual this is -1, which is impossible. So the boundary is compressible, and since M is irreducible, M is a solid torus. This is RR's own observation after Def 7.2 (||Y|| <= g_Y - 2) specialized to g_Y = 1, and RR's introduction says such manifolds with H_1 = Z are boundary compressible.

(5) The argument is consistent with GSTs that are not solid tori:
- N_g and nontrivial closed-braid complements in S^1xS^2 have H_1 = Z+Z/g with g >= 2, which the torsion-free hypothesis excludes.
- S^1xD^2 # (Poincare sphere) is a GST with H_1 = Z, which irreducibility excludes.
- Gillespie (arXiv:1603.05016) independently defines g_Y as ord(i(lambda)) and uses the same compressing-disk mechanism.

In this case both imported facts (H_1(M) = Z and irreducibility) can also be re-derived from the actual fillings alone. Only the minor items below remain: a wording slip and some hypotheses that should be stated explicitly.

sources_checked.source: Rasmussen-Rasmussen, Floer simple manifolds and L-space intervals, arXiv:1508.05900v2 (24 Nov 2015)
sources_checked.statement_paraphrase: Standing assumption: Y is a rational homology S^1xD^2 with H_1 = Z+T and phi the projection to the free part. g_Y > 0 is the index of the image in Z (printed 'im phi = g_Y Z', evidently meaning the image of H_1(boundary)). Equivalent descriptions: the minimal intersection of a boundary curve with a generating surface of H_2(Y, boundary); the minimal number of boundary components of such a surface; the order of the homological longitude l in H_1(Y). k_Y is the order of T/(T cap im iota), so |T| = k_Y g_Y.
sources_checked.note: M is a rational homology solid torus with T = 0, so g_M = k_M = 1 under every listed description and by |T| = k g. The proof's 'order of the homological longitude' reading is one of RR's stated equivalents. Under the literal misprint (phi surjective), g = 1 as well.

sources_checked.statement_paraphrase: A generalized solid torus is a Floer simple manifold whose Delta-bar has degree strictly less than g_Y (the overline is present in the PDF; pdftotext drops it).
sources_checked.note: This is exactly the proof's 'Floer simplicity and degree(bar-Delta(M)) < g_M'.

sources_checked.location: Section 2.1, p. 6 (definitions of tau-bar, Delta-bar, normalization)
sources_checked.statement_paraphrase: tau is normalized with no terms of negative phi-degree and a nonzero constant term. tau-bar is its image under phi and Delta-bar = (1-t)*tau-bar. Delta-bar can differ from the Alexander polynomial, e.g. Z#(S^1xD^2) with b_1(Z)=0 has Delta = 0 but Delta-bar = |H_1(Z)|.
sources_checked.note: Delta-bar(M) is a polynomial with nonzero constant term, so it is nonzero. deg < 1 forces degree 0, as the proof says.

sources_checked.location: Proposition 7.8 and proof, pp. 45-46 (Z introduced on p. 45 as a rational homology sphere)
sources_checked.statement_paraphrase: If a knot in Z#(S^1xS^2) has an L-space surgery, its complement is a GST. The proof uses the Ai-Peters twisted exact triangle to show that all non-longitudinal slopes are L-space slopes, reducing to the distance-one case by a connected sum with a lens-space core. A torsion product formula then gives tau-bar ~ |H_1(Z)|(1-t^g)/(1-t)^2.
sources_checked.note: Z = S^3, M(lambda) = S^1xS^2 from the actual unlink closure, and the other probe's actual closure gives a lens space (S^3 if at distance one), which is an L-space. The meridian lambda of K' is automatically M's homological longitude, since b_1(M(lambda)) = 1 and M has a QHS filling. With Z = S^3 and g = 1 the proof's formula gives tau-bar(M) ~ 1/(1-t), so bar-Delta(M) ~ 1.

sources_checked.statement_paraphrase: For boundary-incompressible Floer simple Y, the Thurston norm of a generator of H_2(Y, boundary) equals deg Delta-bar minus 1. If Y is also irreducible, Y fibers iff Delta-bar is monic.
sources_checked.note: The norm clause needs only boundary incompressibility (assumed for contradiction) and Floer simplicity (from the GST), so it yields norm -1, which is impossible. The underlying norm-detection results usually assume irreducibility, but M is irreducible anyway.

sources_checked.statement_paraphrase: For a GST, Cor 2.3 gives norm <= g_Y - 2, and a generating surface has at least g_Y boundary components, so it has genus 0. Cor 7.4: Delta-bar ~ k_Y(1 - t^{g_Y})/(1-t).
sources_checked.note: With g = k = 1: Delta-bar ~ 1, and norm <= -1 is impossible unless the boundary is compressible. This matches the proof's argument.

sources_checked.statement_paraphrase: The authors remark that a Floer simple manifold with empty D^tau is easily seen to be boundary compressible when H_1 is Z, or more generally when it is semi-primitive.
sources_checked.note: This independently confirms the compressibility conclusion in the H_1 = Z case.

sources_checked.statement_paraphrase: N_g = M(empty; 1/g, -1/g) has H_1 = Z+Z/g and all non-longitudinal fillings are L-spaces. An irreducible semi-primitive GST is the complement of a closed g_Y-strand braid in S^1xS^2.
sources_checked.note: These are GSTs that are not solid tori, and all have torsion Z/g with g >= 2, so g_M = 1 excludes them. With g = 1, Cor 7.12 would also give a 1-braid complement, i.e. a solid torus, but its proof is degenerate at g = 1, so the proof's Cor 2.3 route is cleaner. S^1xD^2 # (Poincare sphere) is a GST with H_1 = Z excluded only by irreducibility, which confirms the proof's remark that both hypotheses are needed.

sources_checked.statement_paraphrase: An L-space is a QHS^3 whose hat-HF has rank one in each Spin^c structure. Floer simple means some filling core is a Floer simple knot. Having more than one L-space filling is equivalent to being Floer simple.
sources_checked.note: Lens spaces and S^3 are L-spaces, and the L-space property does not depend on orientation.

sources_checked.source: T. Gillespie, L-space fillings and generalized solid tori, arXiv:1603.05016v1
sources_checked.statement_paraphrase: Defines g_Y as the order of the image of the homological longitude, and a GST exactly as in RR. Shows solid-torus-like manifolds have g_Y = 1, so a genus-0 generator is a disk and the boundary is compressible.
sources_checked.note: Independent corroboration of the reading of g_Y and of the g = 1 compressing-disk mechanism. Text at /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-calebbarnett/7610ac96-4d03-4d32-b526-8a5647837809/scratchpad/gill/g.txt.

findings.claim: The actual shared product at this slope is the two-component unlink, so M(lambda)=S^1 x S^2.
findings.why: 'Product' is a wording slip. What is meant is the common closure link C_lambda(X) = C_lambda(R), whose double branched cover is S^1xS^2. The mathematics is unaffected.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace 'shared product' with 'shared closure link'.

findings.claim: By [RR, Proposition 7.8], this exterior is a generalized solid torus.
findings.why: RR state Prop 7.8 for a knot in Z#(S^1xS^2), with Z introduced in the preceding sentence as a rational homology sphere. Their proof writes Y(l) = Z#(S^1xS^2), which implicitly requires the knot's meridian to be the complement's homological longitude. The proof does not spell out that Z = S^3, that the L-space surgery is M(alpha_2) (a lens space, or S^3 at distance one), or that lambda is M's homological longitude. All three are automatic: b_1(M(lambda)) = 1 and M has a QHS filling. Stating them keeps a reader from suspecting a hypothesis mismatch.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one sentence. Here Z = S^3. The core K' of the lambda-filling has the lens-space (or S^3) surgery M(alpha_2), and its meridian lambda is the homological longitude of M. Optionally note that the torsion formula in RR's proof of 7.8 (or Cor 7.4) gives bar-Delta(M) ~ 1 directly.

findings.claim: In RR's notation, the order g_M of the homological longitude in H_1(M) is 1, because H_1(M)=Z and the longitude represents zero.
findings.why: RR's formal definition of g_Y (p. 42) is the index of the image of boundary homology in H_1/T. It is printed as 'im phi = g_Y Z', where phi is the surjective projection, an evident misprint. 'Order of the homological longitude' is one of RR's stated equivalents. The proof's value is correct under every reading, but citing only the equivalent invites a quibble about the misprinted primary definition.
findings.suggested_fix: Also cite RR's identity |T| = k_M g_M from the Section 7 preamble: T = 0 forces g_M = k_M = 1. Alternatively cite Gillespie's g_Y = ord(i(lambda)). No change to the argument is needed.

findings.claim: The boundary is compressible, and irreducibility from Step 2 makes M a solid torus. (Also the use of H_1(M)=Z from Step 2.)
findings.why: Step 4 imports H_1(M) = Z and irreducibility from Step 2, which uses the determinant of the auxiliary mu-closure and so Step 1's bracket-vector equality. In the lambda-probe case both facts follow from the actual fillings alone. M(lambda) = S^1xS^2 forces T to be cyclic of order g_M, generated by the longitude. Then |H_1(M(alpha_2))| = g_M^2 * Delta(alpha_2, lambda) must equal |H_1(V(alpha_2))| = Delta(alpha_2, lambda), so g_M = 1 and H_1(M) = Z. S^1xS^2 is prime and b_1(M) = 1, so M is irreducible. This is not a defect. It is a cheap way to make Step 4 independent of Steps 1-2 (only Step 5 still needs [X]=[R]).
findings.suggested_fix: Optionally add this two-line derivation of H_1(M)=Z and irreducibility in the lambda-probe case, so Step 4 does not depend on the determinant argument of Step 2.

audit:S3b-floer-simple-endpoint.summary: This half of Step 3 holds. Each RR result it uses says what the proof needs, under hypotheses M satisfies. (1) Two lens-space fillings at distinct slopes give Floer simplicity by RR Prop 1.3, which needs only a compact oriented manifold with torus boundary: no irreducibility or incompressibility. (2) RR's normalization (Introduction p.2, Section 2.1 p.6, Prop 2.2) together with Prop 1.4 gives tau(M) = sum a_n t^n with a_n in {0,1}, a_0 = 1, and a_n = 1 for large n. No torsion-free hypothesis is needed, and the orientation of t is fixed by phi(mu) > 0, which is harmless here because Delta_K is symmetric. (3) Since H_1(M) = Z, the projection Phi is the identity and tau ~ Delta(M)/(1-t) (RR Section 2.1). So bar-Delta(M) = D = t^h Delta_K, with the sign forced because D(1) = 1 = Delta_K(1). (4) The coefficient argument is correct: alternating +1,-1,...,+1, an odd number of terms, a nonzero central term, and Delta''(1) = 2 sum (-1)^(k-j) n_j^2 > 0 unless Delta = 1. I checked this by hand and by enumerating every 0/1 torsion sequence up to degree 16 (765 symmetric cases, no violations). (5) RR Corollary 2.3 (p.7) states that a boundary-incompressible Floer simple Y has ||Y|| = deg bar-Delta(Y) - 1, where ||Y|| is the Thurston norm of a generator of H_2(Y,dY). Irreducibility is required only for its fibration clause, and its source, Ni's Theorem 1.1 and Remark 1.2, also has no irreducibility hypothesis. With D = 1 the formula gives -1, which is impossible, so dM compresses. With irreducibility, which I rechecked from Step 2 via uniqueness of prime decomposition, M is a solid torus. RR independently remark (p.3) that a Floer simple Y with D^tau(Y) empty and H_1(Y) = Z is boundary compressible, and tau = 1/(1-t) gives D^tau(M) empty, so this agrees. Only the homeomorphism type of the fillings in (1) matters here; the orientation-sensitive part of (1) is not used. What I found are citation and attribution slips only. Not audited here: the inputs from Step 2 (H_1(M) = Z, that Y is an integral homology sphere, the lens-space fillings) and from the first half of Step 3 (Delta''(1) = 0).

sources_checked.statement_paraphrase: L(Y) is the set of slopes giving L-space fillings of a compact connected oriented 3-manifold with torus boundary; if L(Y) is nonempty then b_1(Y)=1. Y is Floer simple if some filling's core is a Floer simple knot, meaning rank HFK = |H_1| (equivalently, the ambient manifold is an L-space and the spectral sequence to HF-hat degenerates).
sources_checked.note: M is the double branched cover of B^3 over two arcs: compact, connected, oriented, with torus boundary. Irreducibility and boundary incompressibility are not standing assumptions.

sources_checked.location: Proposition 1.3, p.2; proof in Section 3.1 (Lemmas 3.2, 3.3 and Corollary 3.4), pp.10-12
sources_checked.statement_paraphrase: Y has more than one L-space filling slope if and only if Y is Floer simple. The proof uses the core of one L-space filling, a knot in an L-space with another L-space surgery, and shows its HFK consists of coherent chains.
sources_checked.note: M(alpha_1) and M(alpha_2) are lens spaces (possibly S^3) at distinct slopes, since q_1/p_1 != q_2/p_2, so |L(M)| >= 2. Only the homeomorphism type of the fillings is needed.

sources_checked.location: Section 1, normalization paragraph immediately before Proposition 1.4, p.2
sources_checked.statement_paraphrase: With phi the projection of H_1(Y) = Z + T onto Z, tau(Y) can be normalized to a sum over h with phi(h) >= 0, with a_0 nonzero and a_h = 1 for all but finitely many h with phi(h) > 0. When H_1(Y) = Z, tau(Y) = Delta(Y)/(1-t), with Delta(Y) normalized to lie in Z[t] and the denominator expanded in positive powers of t.
sources_checked.note: This, not Proposition 1.4, is the source of the normal form the proof writes down.

sources_checked.statement_paraphrase: If Y is Floer simple, every coefficient a_h of the normalized torsion is 0 or 1.
sources_checked.note: There is no torsion-free hypothesis; the coefficients are indexed by all of H_1(Y). Combined with a_0 != 0 this gives a_0 = 1.

sources_checked.statement_paraphrase: Section 2 sets Y as the complement of an oriented knot in a rational homology sphere, with phi the projection to H_1/T and its sign chosen so that phi(meridian) > 0. tau(Y) lives in a Novikov ring and is determined up to multiplication by elements of H_1(Y); it is normalized to vanish where phi < 0 and to have a_0 nonzero. For H_1(Y) = Z, tau(Y) ~ Delta(Y)/(1-t), described as well known. bar-tau = Phi(tau) and bar-Delta = (1-t) bar-tau, where Phi is induced by phi. Example: Z#(S^1 x D^2) has Delta = 0 but bar-Delta = |H_1(Z)|.
sources_checked.note: H_1(M) = Z and the meridian of K generates it, so Phi is the identity and bar-Delta(M) = D. Delta(M) = Delta_K because Y is an integral homology sphere. The sign is fixed by D(1) = 1 = Delta_K(1). The Z#(S^1 x D^2) example is the reducible case with bar-Delta = 1, which the proof's irreducibility argument excludes.

sources_checked.source: Rasmussen-Rasmussen, arXiv:1508.05900v2 (citing Turaev, Torsions of 3-dimensional manifolds, Lemma II.4.5.1 and Theorem II.4.2.1)

audit:S1-scope-and-bracket.summary: The proof's STATEMENT matches Sikora's Conjecture 2 (arXiv v2), which is Conjecture 1.2 in the published version, with nothing weakened. P and Q are Sikora's T1 and T2: framed rational tangles that differ as unframed tangles (Section 4.1). By Conway's bijection, "distinct unframed slopes" means the same thing. C_P(X) is N(X+P), equality is balanced isotopy (Section 4), and X=R is the conjecture's uniqueness claim. One harmless strengthening: Section 4 defines a framed tangle as exactly two bands, while the proof lets X have closed components, which Step 2 rules out. Step 1 is correct. Theorem 21's proof writes [N(X+T_i)] as row_i(B) times [X], with det B = (delta^2-1) times det([T1]0 [T1]inf; [T2]0 [T2]inf). This is nonzero for distinct rational probes (Cor. 19); I checked the closure expansion against the PDF figure. Figure 5 shows that the balanced first move adds or removes a pair of opposite kinks on parallel strands, so the bracket is a balanced-isotopy invariant. The closures therefore have exactly equal brackets, and [X]=[R] holds exactly, not just up to a unit. The normalization is also right. Sikora sets [U^0]=1, and his proof of Prop. 26 uses det(L)=|[L]| at A=e^{pi i/4}. delta vanishes there, so dividing by delta first is needed in the other convention. Framing factors and the A to A^{-1} sign convention do not change the modulus. A numerical check found no mismatch (3000 random rational tangles; 5252 distinct-slope pairs, det B nonzero in every case). What remains is citation and presentation fixes only.

audit:S3a-signed-surgery-cassonwalker.summary:
Step 3a holds. I found no gap.

**Orientation and sign.** Sikora's balanced isotopy (Sec. 4, Fig. 5) is built from three diagram moves:
- cancelling a pair of curls on two strands;
- Reidemeister II;
- Reidemeister III.

Each is an ambient isotopy of the underlying unframed links, so each hypothesis gives an orientation-preserving homeomorphism of S^3. Its lift to the double branched covers is also orientation-preserving.

The identification of dM with dV covers the identity of the 4-punctured Conway sphere. Any such identification is either the identity or the elliptic involution, which acts by -I on homology. A Dehn twist (shear) would have to cover a nontrivial mapping class of the sphere, so none can appear. The involution sends (p,q) to (-p,-q) and fixes every slope and every ratio p/q.

The torus T gets the same boundary orientation from M and from V, because both orientations are pulled back from dB. So one oriented pair (mu, lambda) meets the p/q sign convention for K in Y and for U in S^3 simultaneously. The closing solid torus is common to both closures, and either lift of the gluing gives the same closed manifold. Equation (1), with the same signed coefficient on both sides, is therefore correct. That orientation is preserved matters: under a mirror identification the equations would pick up 2*lambda(L(p_i,q_i)) terms and would not force Delta''(1) = 0.

**Casson-Walker.** Ni-Wu, Proposition 3.1 / eq. (7) (Sec. 3.1, journal p. 9; same numbering in arXiv v2) does state the formula for a null-homologous knot in any rational homology sphere. Their conventions:
- L(p,q) is defined as p/q surgery on the unknot in S^3;
- normalization lambda(S^3_{+1}(right-handed trefoil)) = 1;
- Delta symmetric with Delta(1) = 1.

Ni-Wu give no proof. They call it a special case of a more general formula and point to Boyer-Lines, Theorem 2.8. The restatements I found give that theorem only for knots in integral homology spheres; the general rational case rests on Walker. Step 2 makes Y an integral homology sphere, so Boyer-Lines covers exactly the case used.

**The subtraction.** It forces Delta_K''(1) = 0 whatever the normalization. In any consistent version of the formula, the lens-space term must equal lambda(S^3_{p/q}(U)) in that source's own conventions (apply the formula to the unknot in S^3), so it cancels exactly. Rescaling, or flipping the sign of the Delta'' term, multiplies every term by the same nonzero constant. Walker's general formula gives the same result: its tau correction depends only on intersection data on the boundary torus, which is identical for M and V. As a check, (7) gives lambda(S^3_5(RHT)) = 1/10 = lambda(-L(5,1)), which agrees with the known identification by d-invariants.

**Limitation.** I could not open Boyer-Lines (the GDZ link returned no PDF) or Walker's book. I checked both through restatements by Ni-Wu, Ichihara-Jong, Ichihara-Ito-Saito, Z. Wu (2009) and Ravelomanana.

The four findings below are all minor: citation precision, an unstated normalization, and two sentences that should be spelled out.

Normalization: lambda of +1 surgery on the right-handed trefoil is 1 (Casson scaling). Delta_K is symmetric with Delta_K(1) = 1. Prop 3.3 gives lambda(L(p,q)) = -s(q,p)/2, where the Dedekind sum carries sign(p). Ni-Wu state Prop 3.1 without proof, as a special case of a more general surgery formula, citing Boyer-Lines Theorem 2.8.

Hypotheses hold: Y is an integral homology sphere (Step 2), so K is null-homologous; p_i != 0, so the surgered manifold is a rational homology sphere. Ni-Wu's L(p,q) is literally S^3_{p/q}(U), the right side of (1), so the lens terms cancel by definition. Uses lambda(Y_K(p/q)) = lambda(Y) + lambda(L(p,q)) + (q/2p) Delta_K''(1) for knots in an integral homology sphere, citing Saveliev, Invariants for homology 3-spheres, Cor. 4.5.

findings.claim: The Casson-Walker surgery formula [NW, Proposition 3.1] applies to a null-homologous knot in any rational homology sphere, including Y.
findings.why: This accurately paraphrases Ni-Wu Prop. 3.1 / eq. (7), Sec. 3.1. But Ni-Wu state it without proof and attribute it to Boyer-Lines Theorem 2.8, which by its restatements covers knots in integral homology spheres only; the general rational-homology-sphere case rests on Walker's formula. So the proof leans on a secondary restatement whose own attribution is loose for the generality claimed. There is no mathematical consequence, because Step 2 makes Y an integral homology sphere.
findings.suggested_fix: Cite Boyer-Lines, J. reine angew. Math. 405 (1990), Theorem 2.8 (knots in integral homology spheres) as the primary source. Add Walker (1992) for the general formula and keep [NW, Prop. 3.1, (7)] as a convenient restatement. Replace 'any rational homology sphere, including Y' with 'an integral homology sphere, which Y is by Step 2'.

findings.claim: 0 = lambda_CW(Y) + (q_i/(2p_i))*Delta_K''(1), i=1,2.
findings.why: The proof never fixes the normalization of lambda_CW. The coefficient q/(2p) is right only in Ni-Wu's Casson scaling, where lambda(S^3_{+1}(right-handed trefoil)) = 1 and Delta is symmetric with Delta(1) = 1. Other sources differ: Z. Wu (arXiv:0911.5333, Prop. 2.2) has coefficient -(q/p) with lambda(L(p,q)) = s(q,p). The conclusion Delta''(1) = 0 does not depend on this. In any consistent version the lens term equals lambda(S^3_{p/q}(U)) and cancels exactly against the right side of (1), and rescaling or a sign change multiplies every term by the same nonzero constant. Still, the displayed equation is literally correct only in one normalization.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one sentence: 'Normalize as in [NW]: lambda(S^3_{+1}(right-handed trefoil)) = 1, Delta symmetric with Delta(1) = 1, L(p,q) = S^3_{p/q}(U). Any other normalization rescales the Delta'' term by a fixed nonzero constant, which does not affect the subtraction.'

findings.claim: Both covers inherit orientation from the same oriented tangle ball, and the boundary identification preserves orientation.
findings.why:
I verified this is correct, but the step from it to 'same signed p/q' is left implicit. The missing links are:
- The sign convention for p/q (the sign of mu.lambda relative to the exterior's boundary orientation) depends only on how T is oriented as the boundary of the exterior.
- That orientation is the same for dM and dV, since both are pulled back from dB (outward normals map to outward normals), so a lift of the identity on dB preserves orientation.
- No shear can occur: an identification covering the identity of the 4-punctured sphere is either the identity or the elliptic involution -I, while a Dehn twist would have to cover a nontrivial mapping class.
- The closing solid torus is common to both closures, and both lifts of the gluing give the same closed manifold, because the deck involution extends over that solid torus.
This matters because orientation preservation carries the argument: under a mirror identification the equations become lambda(Y) + 2*lambda(L(p_i,q_i)) + (q_i/2p_i)Delta'' = 0, which do not force Delta'' = 0.
findings.suggested_fix: Add: 'The sign convention for p/q surgery depends only on the orientation of the peripheral torus as the boundary of the exterior. dM and dV both carry the orientation pulled back from dB, and any identification covering the identity of the 4-punctured sphere is the identity or -I. Hence the same oriented pair (mu, lambda) is a standard meridian-longitude pair for both K in Y and U in S^3.'

findings.claim: A link isotopy lifts to an orientation-preserving map of the closed covers.
findings.why: The hypothesis is Sikora's balanced isotopy (Sec. 4, Fig. 5), which Sikora calls more flexible than standard framed isotopy: the paired-curl move can shift framing between strands. The proof should say why this still yields an ambient isotopy. Each balanced move is an R1 pair, RII or RIII on the unframed diagram, so a balanced isotopy is an orientation-preserving ambient isotopy of the underlying unframed links in R^3 inside S^3. The statement is true, so there is no gap, but the proof never makes this bridge explicit.
findings.suggested_fix: Insert before the sentence: 'Each balanced Reidemeister move of [S, Fig. 5] is a pair of R1 moves, an RII or an RIII on the unframed diagram. A balanced isotopy is therefore an ambient isotopy of S^3 carrying C_P(X) onto C_P(R).'

audit:S5-recovery-and-coverage.summary:
Step 5 holds, and the case analysis covers every case.

1. Buck–Mauricio record the criterion as an unconditional equivalence for a ball with exactly two properly embedded arcs: rational if and only if the double branched cover is a solid torus. It needs no primeness or local-knot assumption and says nothing about the deck involution. Step 2 supplies the two-arc hypothesis: the mu-closure has determinant 1, and a c-component link has determinant divisible by 2^(c-1). I re-derived that fact from the Conway polynomial.

2. Sikora's Corollary 20 compares two framed rational tangles only; the proof correctly avoids the much stronger Theorem 24(c), which is equivalent to the Jones conjecture. Theorem 21 gives the exact equality [X]=[R], so once X is rational, X=R under balanced isotopy. Sikora's Figure 5 confirms that balanced moves cancel opposite kinks on two separate strands, so only the total framing matters. This last deduction is exactly Sikora's own Proposition 1.

3. The case split is exhaustive: both probe slopes differ from lambda (Step 3), or exactly one equals it (Step 4). Both cannot, since the slopes are distinct.
- Probes whose R-closures are unknots (p=+-1, giving S^3) are covered by Step 3.
- One probe at lambda with the other giving S^3 is covered by Step 4. RR Proposition 7.8 requires only a knot in Z#(S^1 x S^2) with an L-space surgery; here Z=S^3.
- Y=S^3 is never assumed: Ni–Wu Proposition 3.1 is stated for a null-homologous knot in any rational homology sphere.
- Y being an L-space is never assumed: Floer simplicity comes from RR Proposition 1.3, using the two actual lens-space fillings.
- Primeness and absence of local knots are never assumed: irreducibility is derived in Step 2 from H_1(M)=Z plus an actual lens-space filling.

4. The proof never replaces an actual homeomorphism with equality of invariants. Determinants are used only for homology orders, where they are exact: the longitude identification and Y being an integral homology sphere. Every lens space and S^1 x S^2 identification comes from an actual link isotopy lifted to the covers.

The two minor issues are both in Step 5's citations:
- (a) Nothing is cited for passing from "pair homeomorphic to the trivial tangle" to "isotopic rel boundary to Conway's tangle in the marked ball". Buck–Mauricio Theorem 3.6 plus the Alexander trick fills this.
- (b) Only Buck–Mauricio's recording of the Lickorish attribution could be checked. The AMS copy of the original was behind a bot check, which I did not bypass.

sources_checked.statement_paraphrase: Def 3.1: a tangle is a 3-ball with a pair of properly embedded arcs and an orientation-preserving boundary parametrization. Def 3.4(2): it is rational if the pair is homeomorphic to (D^2 x I, two points x I), ignoring the parametrization. Thm 3.5(2), attributed to Lickorish [34]: a tangle is rational if and only if its double branched cover is a solid torus. There is no primeness hypothesis and no condition on the involution; the text notes the cover is unique because the ball is contractible.
sources_checked.note: The only hypothesis is two arcs and no closed components. Step 2 supplies it: det(C_mu(X))=1 is odd, so C_mu(X) is a knot. I re-derived the divisibility of det by 2^(c-1) from nabla_L(z)=z^(c-1)p(z^2), det=|nabla_L(2i)|; I did not check the [St] numbering. The proof's remark about the deck involution is accurate but is not in BM's text, and it is harmless.

sources_checked.statement_paraphrase: Every parametrized rational tangle is isomorphic to some T(p/q), and two T(p/q) are isomorphic exactly when the fractions agree. Isomorphism means a homeomorphism compatible with the boundary parametrizations.
sources_checked.note: The proof does not cite this, but it is needed to go from BM's homeomorphism-level rationality to Sikora's marked Conway tangle up to isotopy rel boundary. An isomorphism is the identity on the boundary, so by the Alexander trick it is isotopic to the identity. See finding 1.

sources_checked.statement_paraphrase: Two framed rational tangles with the same bracket vector are equal. Proof: equal KB ratios give the same fraction (Corollary 19, evaluation at q=1), so the tangles differ only by n framing twists. The bracket then scales by (-A)^(3n), forcing n=0.
sources_checked.note: Both tangles must be rational, and the proof uses it only after Step 5 shows X is rational. It does not misuse it as Theorem 24(c), the bracket detecting a rational tangle among all tangles, which is equivalent to the Jones conjecture. The fraction is computed in the fixed marked basis, so the marking is respected.

The coefficient matrix has determinant (delta^2-1) times det[[T1]0,[T1]inf;[T2]0,[T2]inf], which is nonzero. Sikora remarks that Theorem 21 and Corollary 20 together give Proposition 1: at most one framed rational solution.

A framed rational tangle is a rational tangle with any framing. T1 and T2 are assumed to differ as unframed tangles.

findings.claim: Step 5: 'The classical branched-cover criterion makes X rational [BM, Theorem 3.5(2)] ... Finally, [S, Corollary 20] distinguishes balanced framed rational tangles by their bracket vectors.'
findings.why: BM's 'rational' (Def 3.4(2)) only says the pair is homeomorphic to the trivial tangle, ignoring the boundary parametrization. Sikora's Corollary 20 compares Conway rational tangles in the fixed marked ball, up to balanced isotopy rel boundary. The proof needs one more step: a parametrized rational tangle is isomorphic to some T(p/q) (BM Theorem 3.6, Conway). Such an isomorphism is the identity on the boundary, so by the Alexander trick it is isotopic to the identity rel boundary. Carrying X's framing along, X is balanced-isotopic to a Conway rational tangle with some number of twists. This step is standard and true but neither stated nor cited.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one sentence: 'By Conway's classification [BM, Theorem 3.6] and the Alexander trick, X is isotopic rel boundary to a Conway rational tangle, so X with its framing is a framed rational tangle in Sikora's sense.' Then cite Corollary 20, or simply Sikora's Proposition 1 (at most one framed rational solution), which is exactly Theorem 21 plus Corollary 20.

findings.claim: [BM] reference: 'Records the classical solid-torus-cover/rational-tangle criterion, attributed there to W. B. R. Lickorish, Prime knots and tangles (1981).'
findings.why: I verified only the secondary recording, BM Theorem 3.5(2), which is stated without hypotheses beyond two arcs in a ball. Lickorish's original could not be checked here. The solid-torus-implies-rational direction classically relies on the equivariant Dehn lemma (Meeks–Yau; Kim–Tollefson) and Waldhausen's Z/2 Smith theorem, so a referee may want a primary proof cited. This is a citation-robustness issue, not a logical one: Sikora uses the same implication in proving his own Lemma 14, and other tangle papers state it.

candidates.construction: Ernst-Sumners / Sikora Lemma 14-15 unframed pair: R = <inf>, X = <-1/2>, probes T1 = <0>, T2 = <1>. Both tangles give the unknot under both closures.
candidates.outcome: Not a framed counterexample. Sikora v2 Lemma 15: <inf>^f lifts to a framed solution only when the framing gap m-n is 1, and <-1/2>^f only when m-n is -3. So no single framed system has both as solutions, and Proposition 1 (Thm 21 + Cor 20) is proved. The proof blocks this pair at Steps 1-2. [X] != [R], and at the lambda_R closure (+<inf>), R gives the 2-component unlink (det 0) while X gives the Hopf link (det |ad+bc| = 2). No framed variant survives.

candidates.construction: Framing redistribution: X = R with one extra positive twist on arc 1 and one extra negative twist on arc 2, with probes chosen so that both closures of R are knots.
candidates.outcome: Under ordinary framed isotopy rel boundary, this X solves the system and differs from R, so the theorem would be false. Sikora Sec. 4 uses balanced isotopy instead. I rasterized Fig. 5 from the arXiv source in memory: opposite kinks on different strands cancel, and twist location does not matter. That makes X = R. Cor 20's proof only controls the total twist number, which is consistent. The candidate states the balanced convention in both hypothesis and conclusion, so this is not a counterexample, but the convention is essential.

candidates.construction: Orientation-reversed lens surgery. The trefoil exterior is Sigma2(X) via the Montesinos trick (strong inversion), with lambda the Seifert longitude. Then S^3_5(T2,3) = L(5,4), which is -L(5,1) = -S^3_5(U). Also S^3_7(T2,3) = L(7,4), homeomorphic to L(7,2).
candidates.outcome: Fails the hypothesis. N(X+S_5) is the mirror of N(R+S_5) = 5_1, which is chiral, and isotopy preserves ambient orientation. L(7,2) is not homeomorphic to L(7,1) at all. Casson-Walker check: lambda(S^3_5(T)) = -1/10 + 2/10 = +1/10 = -lambda(L(5,1)), consistent with the orientation reversal. I checked the sign bookkeeping in (1) independently. M and V cover the same oriented ball, so they induce the same orientation on the common torus. The deck involution is -I, which preserves orientation and slopes. The signed coefficients in (1) are therefore correct.

candidates.construction: Dual knots in homology spheres: Y = S^3_{1/n}(J) with K* the dual knot, e.g. J = right-handed trefoil, so Y is a Brieskorn homology sphere.
candidates.outcome: There is exactly one orientation-preserving match, Y_{-1/n}(K*) = S^3 = S^3_{-1/n}(U), with K* nontrivial. So one equation is not enough. V(alpha) depends only on alpha relative to lambda, so a second match at K*-slope a/(b-na) is equivalent to S^3_{a/b}(J) = S^3_{a/b}(U), which KMOS excludes. The paired Casson-Walker equations also fail, since lambda(Y) = (n/2)Delta''_J(1) = n != 0.

candidates.construction: Reducible Floer-simple manifolds with H1 = Z and Delta = 1. Example: X = R # T(3,5) as a local knot, so M = V # P with P = Sigma2(T(3,5)) the Poincare sphere. Also X = R # J with J a hypothetical nontrivial Jones-trivial knot.
candidates.outcome: M = (S^1xD^2) # P is Floer simple (every non-longitudinal filling L(p,q) # P is an L-space), has H1 = Z and Delta = 1, and is not a solid torus. So Steps 3-4 genuinely need irreducibility. Step 2 supplies it correctly: an actual lens-space filling is prime, so closed homology-sphere summands are S^3. The isotopy hypothesis fails anyway, since N(X+T_i) = N(R+T_i) # J != N(R+T_i). With J Jones-trivial, [X] = [R] could hold while the actual closures differ. This matches the candidate's remark that the argument does not give Jones unknot detection.

candidates.construction: Generalized solid tori that are not solid tori: N_g = M(empty; 1/g, -1/g) for g >= 2 (g = 2 is the twisted I-bundle over the Klein bottle), and exteriors of Berge / Baker-Buck-Lecuona knots in S^1xS^2 with lens-space surgeries.
candidates.outcome: All of these have H1 = Z + Z/g, where g is the winding number and g >= 2. RR Prop 1.9 notes that such S^1xS^2 knot complements are Floer simple of genus 0. The framed bracket gives closures of determinant 0 and 1, which forces H1(M) = Z and g_M = 1. Then Def 7.2 forces deg bar-Delta = 0, and Cor 2.3 forces a compressing disk. So the homological input excludes them, as the candidate's Step 4 caveat says.

candidates.construction: Knots in homology spheres other than S^3 with Casson invariant 0, with two lens-space surgeries matching the unknot's. Examples: Y = P # -P (an L-space homology sphere with lambda = 0), or a Berge exterior M = S^3 - P(-2,3,7) with lens fillings at 18 and 19.
candidates.outcome: No example survives. The paired Casson-Walker equations force Delta''(1) = 0. RR Props 1.3 and 1.4 make Delta alternating with +-1 coefficients, so Delta = 1. Cor 2.3 then rules out an incompressible boundary, so M is a solid torus and Y = S^3. For the Berge exterior, distance data alone does not pin down lambda: besides lambda_K, the slope 684/37 is at distance 18 and 19 from the two fillings. Step 2 excludes it, because that closure of X has det 684 while the corresponding closure of R has det 0. Taking V's meridian = lambda_K instead, KMOS rules out the match. This shows Step 2's determinant identification of lambda is load-bearing.

candidates.construction: Tangles with closed components, e.g. R together with a split or linked unknotted loop.
candidates.outcome: Excluded by definition: Sikora's framed tangles are J1xI u J2xI, two ribbons and no loops. Step 2 excludes them independently. A det-1 closure is a knot (Stoimenow Prop 6.5: det is odd iff the link is a knot), and any loop would survive every closure as an extra component. A split loop also multiplies the bracket by delta, so [X] != [R].

G1-counterexample-hunt.weakest_point: The weakest point is the imported Rasmussen-Rasmussen machinery (arXiv:1508.05900v2), which Steps 3-4 depend on entirely. Prop 1.4 supplies the 0/1 torsion coefficients. Cor 2.3 gives ||M|| = deg bar-Delta - 1 for boundary-incompressible Floer-simple M. Prop 7.8 is the only source of Floer simplicity in Step 4, when one probe is the longitude. RR state Cor 2.3 with only a citation to Thurston-norm detection results. The candidate applies it to an irreducible M, where detection (Ni; Juhasz) is established. RR's proof of Prop 7.8 for an L-space slope at distance >= 2 from the longitude is a brief sketch. It converts to integer surgery on K_mu # (lens-space core), then uses the attached cable space to get infinitely many fillings of the original manifold. I reconstructed that sketch and found it sound. The g = 1 torsion computation alone already gives Delta(M) = 1. These are refereed results (Adv. Math. 322, 2017), quoted accurately, so I rate them a concentration of risk rather than a gap. A second dependency: the statement holds only under Sikora's balanced isotopy. Under ordinary framed isotopy, moving framing twists between the two arcs gives an immediate counterexample. The candidate states the convention correctly.
G1-counterexample-hunt.summary:
I read the whole file and did not open any of the excluded files. I checked every cited statement against its primary source, processing fetched material in memory, and created no files. Overall: no counterexample, nothing fatal, and no possible_gap. Every construction I tried violates a hypothesis or is excluded by a correctly cited result.

The argument reduces to two inputs. First, the framed hypothesis gives [X] = [R] by Theorem 21. That yields closure determinants 0 and 1, so H1(M) = Z and lambda is the longitude. Second, the two actual isotopies give oriented lens-space fillings. Framing enters only through Thm 21 and Cor 20.

Citations checked:
- Sikora v2: Conj 2, Sec 4 with the Fig. 5 balanced moves, Cor 20 and Thm 21 match the journal's Conj 1.2, Cor 7.2 and Thm 8.1. I rederived det B = (delta^2-1)*det([Ti]_0, [Ti]_inf).
- Ni-Wu Prop 3.1, eq. (7): stated for null-homologous knots in any rational homology sphere, exactly as used.
- RR: Props 1.3 and 1.4, Cor 2.3, Def 7.2, Prop 7.8, and g_Y as the order of the homological longitude all match. RR also remark that the H1 = Z case is easy, consistent with Steps 3-4.
- Buck-Mauricio Thm 3.5(2): the solid-torus cover criterion, attributed to Lickorish.
- Gainullin Thm 8.2 (pp. 104-105) is described accurately.
- The IPAM abstract still calls the statement a conjecture.

Independent checks: the oriented signed-coefficient identification in (1) is correct. The prime-decomposition proof of irreducibility is correct. The alternating Alexander polynomial argument (Delta''(1) = 2*sum of (-1)^(k-j) n_j^2 > 0 unless Delta = 1) is correct.

Minor issues:
- (a) Stoimenow Prop 6.5 states that det is odd iff the link is a knot. The 2^(c-1) divisibility appears only in its proof. The parity statement already suffices.
- (b) Dasbach et al. Sec. 3 mentions det = |H1(Sigma2)| only in passing and says nothing about det 0 versus infinite H1. The fact is standard but weakly sourced.
- (c) The closed-component paragraph is redundant, since Sikora's framed tangles have exactly two ribbons.
- (d) RR v2 garbles the definition of g_Y ('im phi = g_Y Z' with phi onto). The proof correctly uses the equivalent characterization.

One observation from the Berge test: distance data alone does not fix lambda. The determinant-0 identification in Step 2 is essential, and it is correctly supplied by the bracket.

G4-gainullin-overlap.theorem_paraphrase:
Source: F. Gainullin, Algebraic & Geometric Topology 18 (2018) 69-109, Theorem 8.2. It is first announced on p. 74 as a generalization of the Kronheimer-Mrowka-Ozsvath-Szabo (KMOS) surgery characterization of the unknot (his Thm 1.3). It is restated in Section 8.2 on p. 104 and proved on p. 105. The numbering is the same in arXiv:1504.06180v5.

Setting: Y is a rational homology sphere that is an L-space, and K is a null-homologous knot in Y. L(p,q) means p/q surgery on the unknot in S^3.

Statement: if HF^+ of the p/q surgery Y_{p/q}(K) is isomorphic to HF^+(Y # L(p,q)), then K is the unknot, i.e. it bounds a disk in Y. The isomorphism must respect absolute gradings, because the proof reads the Casson-Walker invariant off HF^+ through d-invariants. Gainullin states the consequence that null-homologous knots in L-spaces are determined by their complements.

Normalization: Delta_K is symmetric with Delta_K(1) = |H_1(Y)|. For an integral homology sphere this is the candidate's normalization.
G4-gainullin-overlap.proof_outline:
Gainullin's proof (p. 105, drawing on Section 4, pp. 84-85, and Section 8.1, pp. 103-104):

(G1) The Casson-Walker invariant is additive under connected sum and is determined by graded HF^+ through Rustamov's formula (his eq. (5), p. 84). So lambda(Y_{p/q}(K)) = lambda(Y) + lambda(L(p,q)).

(G2) His surgery formula (4), p. 84 (Walker Prop. 6.2, normalized as in Ni-Wu) says lambda(Y_{p/q}(K)) = lambda(Y) + lambda(L(p,q)) + q/(2p|H_1(Y)|) Delta_K''(1). Comparing with (G1) gives Delta_K''(1) = 0 from a single slope, because lambda(Y) appears on both sides.

(G3) Y_{p/q}(K) has the HF^+ of an L-space, so it is an L-space. Section 8 extends the Ozsvath-Szabo rational-surgery mapping cone to null-homologous knots in rational homology spheres (Lemma 8.1: H_1 of the exterior is Z plus H_1(Y), with the Z generated by the meridian). With both Y and the surgery L-spaces, every A^+_{(n,h)} is a tower; this uses surjectivity of the tower map for p/q > 0, from his earlier paper, Lemma 12. The algebra of Ozsvath-Szabo, Topology 44 (2005), Section 3, then shows that for each h in H_1(Y) the knot Floer homology has rank at most one in each Alexander grading, with alternating Z/2 gradings and the extreme copies in grading 0. Hence (Section 8.1, p. 104) each Spin^c summand Delta_{K,h} satisfies Delta_{K,h}''(1) >= 0, with equality only if Delta_{K,h} is 1 or t.

(G4) Summing over h, Delta_K''(1) = 0 forces every Delta_{K,h} to be trivial, and symmetry makes each equal to 1. So HFK-hat is supported in Alexander grading 0.

(G5) Ni-Wu, Adv. Math. 267 (2014), Thm 2.2, a reformulation of Ni's Thurston-norm detection, gives g(K) = 0, so K is the unknot.

The candidate's Step 3 follows the same skeleton:

(C1, C2) Two actual orientation-preserving homeomorphisms Y_{r_i}(K) = S^3_{r_i}(U) and Ni-Wu Prop 3.1 give two linear equations, 0 = lambda(Y) + (q_i/2p_i) Delta''(1). Because the slopes are distinct, Delta''(1) = 0 and lambda(Y) = 0.

(C3) The two lens-space fillings make M Floer simple [RR Prop 1.3]. RR Prop 1.4 puts the torsion coefficients in {0,1}, so Delta_K has alternating +1/-1 coefficients. An explicit computation then re-derives Gainullin's Section 8.1 inequality: Delta''(1) > 0 unless Delta = 1.

(C4) Therefore Delta_K = 1.

(C5) RR Cor 2.3 says a boundary-incompressible Floer simple manifold has Thurston norm deg(bar-Delta) - 1, which would be -1 here. So the boundary is compressible, and with irreducibility from Step 2, M is a solid torus.

Both endgames ultimately rest on knot Floer homology detecting the Thurston norm.
G4-gainullin-overlap.key_differences:
1. Hypothesis on the ambient manifold. Theorem 8.2 needs Y to be an L-space. The candidate's Y = M(mu) is only known to be an integral homology sphere, and this cannot be fixed by choosing mu cleverly in advance. By RR Thm 1.6 (arXiv:1508.05900v2), the L-space slopes of the Floer simple M form an interval containing the two probes. A priori that interval need not contain any slope 1/n, i.e. any slope at distance one from lambda. That only becomes clear after tau(M) is known, and computing tau(M) is the output of Step 3. So Step 3 is not a corollary of Theorem 8.2 as stated.

2. Comparison space. Gainullin compares with Y#L(p,q), so lambda(Y) cancels and one slope is enough. The candidate compares with L(p,q) = S^3_{p/q}(U), so lambda(Y) survives. The second slope gives a 2x2 linear system with nonzero determinant (q_1/p_1 - q_2/p_2)/2. The second equation is genuinely needed. Take any nontrivial knot K' in S^3, n != 0, Y = S^3_{1/n}(K'), and K the dual knot in Y. The old meridian of K' is a slope 1/m on the boundary of the exterior (m = -n in one convention), with Y_{1/m}(K) = S^3 = S^3_{1/m}(U). Yet the exterior is not a solid torus. In that example lambda(Y) = (n/2)Delta''(1), which balances the single Casson-Walker equation.

3. The hypothetical where Y is an L-space. Theorem 8.2 still does not apply verbatim. Its hypothesis needs graded HF^+(L(p,q)) to equal HF^+(Y#L(p,q)), which means d(Y) = 0. For an L-space integral homology sphere, Rustamov's formula (Gainullin eq. (5); Ni-Wu Thm 3.5) gives lambda(Y) = -d(Y)/2. So the candidate's second equation, lambda(Y) = 0, is exactly the missing input. In that case Step 3 reduces to: two-slope Casson-Walker, then Rustamov, then Thm 8.2 (K is the unknot in Y), then primality of the lens-space filling (Y = S^3, M a solid torus). If Y = S^3 were known in advance, Step 3 would be a direct one-slope corollary of KMOS Thm 1.1 (Gainullin's Thm 1.3).

4. Floer input. Gainullin's Section 8 mapping cone (Lemma 8.1) requires K to be null-homologous in an L-space. The only L-spaces available to the candidate are the lens-space fillings, and their cores generate H_1 = Z/p_i, so they are not null-homologous when |p_i| > 1. RR Props 1.3-1.4 supply the same alternating structure at the level of the exterior, whichever filling is used. RR Section 3.1 presents this as an extension, via Boileau-Boyer-Cebanu-Walsh, of the Ozsvath-Szabo L-space-knot theorem that Gainullin adapts.

5. Endgame. Gainullin uses Ni-Wu Thm 2.2 genus detection and concludes that K is the unknot in Y. The candidate uses RR Cor 2.3 plus irreducibility from Step 2 and concludes that M is a solid torus, hence Y = S^3. Step 2's irreducibility also covers any irreducibility hypothesis implicit in the norm-detection theorem behind Cor 2.3.

6. Type of hypothesis. Gainullin assumes only a graded Floer homology isomorphism, which is weaker than a homeomorphism. The candidate uses actual orientation-preserving homeomorphisms, which it needs for irreducibility and for the sign matching in (1). I checked the sign matching conceptually: both covers inherit their boundary orientation from the same oriented ball boundary, and the deck involution acts as -I on H_1, so it fixes every slope. It is consistent.

Verification against the sources. Ni-Wu Prop 3.1 (arXiv:1009.4720v2, eq. (7), credited there to Boyer-Lines Thm 2.8) is stated for null-homologous knots in rational homology spheres with Delta(1) = 1, as the candidate claims. For |H_1(Y)| = 1 it agrees with Gainullin's (4). RR Prop 1.3 (more than one L-space slope iff Floer simple), Prop 1.4 (coefficients 0 or 1), Section 2.1 (tau = Delta/(1-t) when H_1 = Z, and the definition of bar-Delta) and Cor 2.3 (boundary incompressible plus Floer simple gives norm = deg bar-Delta - 1) all match the candidate's use.

Issues in Step 3: no possible_gap and nothing fatal found. Minor: (a) the torsion normalization is attributed to RR Prop 1.4, but it is stated in the paragraph before Prop 1.4 and in Section 2.1; (b) Step 3 itself never cites Gainullin, even though it re-derives his Section 8.1 inequality; (c) the original sources of the Casson-Walker formula (Boyer-Lines, Walker) are not cited.

G4-gainullin-overlap.summary:
Gainullin's Theorem 8.2 (AGT 18 (2018), pp. 74, 104-105): if K is a null-homologous knot in an L-space Y and HF^+ of Y_{p/q}(K) matches HF^+(Y#L(p,q)) as graded groups, then K is the unknot. His proof uses the Casson-Walker surgery formula to get Delta''(1) = 0, then the alternating structure of knots with L-space surgeries (Delta''(1) >= 0, with equality only when trivial), then knot Floer genus detection.

The candidate's Step 3 is the same method in a new setting, not a corollary of the theorem:
- Its Y is only an integral homology sphere and cannot be chosen in advance to be an L-space.
- It compares with L(p,q) instead of Y#L(p,q), so lambda(Y) has to be eliminated with a second slope. One slope really is not enough: the dual of 1/n surgery on any nontrivial knot is a counterexample.
- Rasmussen-Rasmussen Floer simplicity of the exterior replaces Gainullin's L-space hypothesis. That substitution is needed because the cores of the lens-space fillings are not null-homologous.
- Even if Y were an L-space, applying Theorem 8.2 would require d(Y) = 0, which the two-slope step supplies.

The cited statements check out against the primary sources: Ni-Wu Prop 3.1; Rasmussen-Rasmussen Props 1.3 and 1.4 and Cor 2.3; Gainullin Theorem 8.2 and Section 8.1. The candidate's own description of Gainullin is accurate.

I found no gap in Step 3. The only problems are minor: Step 3 does not credit Gainullin in line (especially his Section 8.1 inequality), one Rasmussen-Rasmussen citation points to Prop 1.4 instead of the paragraph before it, and the original sources of the Casson-Walker formula are not cited. I did not audit Steps 1, 2, 4 or 5 beyond what Step 3 takes from them.

G2-novelty-keyword-sweep.summary:
I found no existing proof, claimed proof, or announced resolution of Sikora's framed rational-solution uniqueness conjecture (arXiv v2 Conjecture 2, which is CJM Conjecture 1.2).

**Status of the conjecture**
- Sikora's own IPAM abstract (15 Oct 2026) still calls framed uniqueness a conjecture. Its only proven claim is the conditional link to the Jones conjecture.
- His publication page and the arXiv listings through 31 Oct 2026 show no follow-up paper on tangle equations. The 'upcoming work' on the unframed version promised in CJM Sec. 1.1 has not appeared.
- Every paper citing Sikora's paper (7 on Semantic Scholar, 3 on OpenAlex) is about q-rationals. The 2024 erratum only corrects the author's name.
- Coverage limits: Google Scholar was CAPTCHA-blocked, the World Scientific full texts returned 403, and I did not watch the IPAM recording. An unpublished or very recent proof therefore cannot be ruled out.

**Closest prior work and what is new**
- The closest antecedent is Gainullin AGT 2018 Thm 8.2, which uses the same chain: Casson-Walker forces Delta''(1)=0, then alternating coefficients, then genus 0. It needs Y to be an L-space and compares one surgery against Y#L(p,q). The proof describes this accurately.
- The combination in the proof appears nowhere in what I found:
  - Sikora's bracket uniqueness (Thm 21/8.1) gives the determinants of all closures, which forces H_1(M)=Z and fixes the longitude.
  - Two Casson-Walker equations eliminate the unknown lambda(Y).
  - Rasmussen-Rasmussen's Floer-simple torsion and Thurston-norm results replace the L-space hypothesis.
- The individual ingredients are standard. Rasmussen-Rasmussen Prop 7.8 plus Cor 7.12 already settle Step 4 almost immediately. An expert may see the whole argument as a short combination of known tools, but I found no record of it.

**Special cases already known or implied**
- Sikora proves several: at most one framed rational solution, uniqueness of [X], Jones conjecture implies the conjecture (so it holds up to 11 crossings), Prop 1.5, and the framed unknot/unknot systems via Gordon-Luecke.
- Gordon-Luecke covers two unknot closures. Gabai's Property R covers an unknot closure with an unlink closure.
- KMOS, combined with Sikora's Thm 21 to pin the longitude, would give the case with one unknot closure. I found no paper that states this deduction.
- The cyclic surgery theorem plus the Ernst/Darcy classifications handle unframed 4-plat systems at distance 2 or more.
- The DNA-recombination papers solve only specific unframed systems.

**Citation checks**
I checked every cited statement against the primary source, and all match how the proof uses them:
- Rasmussen-Rasmussen Props 1.3, 1.4, 7.8, Cor 2.3 and Def 7.2.
- Ni-Wu Prop 3.1, eq. (7): a null-homologous knot in a rational homology sphere, with Delta(1)=1.
- Gainullin Thm 8.2.
- Buck-Mauricio Thm 3.5(2), which attributes the criterion to Lickorish.
- Sikora's numbering: arXiv Cor 20 and Thm 21 are CJM Cor 7.2 and Thm 8.1, and det B is nonzero even at q=1.

Minor issues only:
- [BM] was published under a different title (MPCPS 2011, 'Connect sum of lens spaces surgeries: application to Hin recombination').
- The torsion normalization the proof attributes to Rasmussen-Rasmussen Prop 1.4 is in the text just before Prop 1.4, not in the proposition itself.

**Sanity check (my own derivation, not from the literature)**
The unframed analogue, CJM Conjecture 1.4, appears to fail. The quotient tangle of the trefoil (by its strong inversion) has an unknot closure and a T(2,5) closure. A rational tangle of slope 1/4 or -1/6 (depending on chirality) has the same two closures. This works because S^3_5(T_{2,3}) = -L(5,1) = S^3_{-5}(U); I confirmed it with Casson-Walker values (0.1 on both sides). This shows that Step 2's bracket-based identification of the longitude is essential, so the candidate proof does not prove too much.

I found no fatal gap in my spot checks. Verdict on priority: no prior proof found.

## 1. Summary

The argument has five parts.

1. **Bracket vector.** Sikora's Theorem 21 says the two framed equations determine the relative bracket vector. So [X] = [R], and every closure of X has the same bracket, and hence the same determinant, as the corresponding closure of R.
2. **Peripheral data.** Let lambda be the disk-bounding slope of V, the double branched cover of R, and let mu be a slope meeting lambda once. The lambda- and mu-closures of X have determinants 0 and 1. Consequences:
   - X has exactly two arcs.
   - Y = M(mu) is an integral homology sphere and H_1(M) = Z.
   - lambda is the preferred longitude of the core K of the mu-filling, matching the longitude of the unknot in S^3 = V(mu).
   - Because M has an actual lens-space filling, M is irreducible.
3. **Neither probe slope is lambda.** The two actual closure isotopies lift to orientation-preserving homeomorphisms Y_{p_i/q_i}(K) = S^3_{p_i/q_i}(U).
   - Two Casson-Walker equations give Delta_K''(1) = 0.
   - Rasmussen-Rasmussen (RR) Floer simplicity forces Delta_K to be alternating, hence Delta_K = 1.
   - RR Corollary 2.3 then forces a compressing disk, so M is a solid torus.
4. **One probe slope is lambda.** RR Proposition 7.8 and Definition 7.2 give the same conclusion.
5. **Conclusion.** Lickorish's criterion makes X rational, and Sikora's Corollary 20 gives X = R.

**Review process.** Six step referees, a counterexample hunter, two novelty sweeps and a comparison with Gainullin reported no fatal finding and no possible gap. Every finding came with a concrete repair, so no adjudication was needed.

## 2. Step-by-step assessment

**Statement and Step 1: holds, minor fixes.**
- The statement is Conjecture 2, and nothing is weakened.
- P and Q play the roles of T_1 and T_2, which Sikora requires to differ as unframed tangles (Sec. 4.1). By Conway's bijection this is the same as "distinct unframed slopes".
- Allowing closed components in X is a harmless strengthening.
- In the proof of Theorem 21, each closure bracket is linear in ([X]_0, [X]_inf). The coefficient determinant factors as (delta^2 - 1) times det([T_i]_0, [T_i]_inf). When the slopes differ this is a nonzero Laurent polynomial (Cor. 19 = CJM Cor. 7.1).
- Balanced moves preserve the bracket, since opposite kinks contribute (-A^3)(-A^-3) = 1. So [X] = [R] holds exactly.
- The normalization paragraph is correct: with unknot value 1, |[L](e^{i pi/4})| = det(L), and delta vanishes at that point.
- Needed: RF1-RF3.

**Step 2: holds, minor fixes.**
- The determinant-1 closure is a knot. Since |H_1| of the double branched cover equals det, with det 0 exactly when H_1 is infinite, Y is an integral homology sphere, H_1(M) = Z, and lambda is the only slope whose filling has infinite H_1.
- This homological identification carries real weight. Distance data alone does not determine lambda: for the Berge exterior with lens fillings at 18 and 19, the slope 684/37 is also at distances 18 and 19.
- The irreducibility argument is correct and needs no Poincare conjecture, but the prime-decomposition case split should be written out (RF6).
- Two citations do not support the claims they are attached to (RF4, RF5).

**Step 3, signed surgery and Casson-Walker: holds, minor fixes.**
- A balanced isotopy is an ambient isotopy of the underlying unframed links.
- dM and dV carry the same boundary orientation, lifted from dB. A lift of the identity is either the identity or -I, and both fix slopes. So (1) holds with the same signed coefficient on each side.
- I checked Ni-Wu Prop. 3.1: null-homologous knot in a rational homology sphere, Delta(1) = 1, L(p,q) defined as p/q surgery on the unknot, normalized by lambda(S^3_{+1}(RHT)) = 1. Ni-Wu attribute it to Boyer-Lines Thm 2.8, which covers the integral homology sphere case used here.
- The lens-space terms cancel, and the distinct ratios q_i/p_i give Delta''(1) = 0.
- **Both slopes are necessary.** Take K the dual of 1/n surgery on any nontrivial knot K'. Then Y_{-1/n}(K) = S^3 = S^3_{-1/n}(U), but the exterior is not a solid torus, and lambda_CW(Y) = (n/2)Delta_{K'}''(1) balances the single equation.
- **Orientation is also necessary.** S^3_5(T_{2,3}) = -L(5,1) shows what a mirror identification would allow.
- Needed: RF7, RF8.

**Step 3, Floer simple endpoint: holds, minor fixes.**
- I checked in RR v2:
  - Prop. 1.3: more than one L-space filling iff Floer simple, with no irreducibility hypothesis.
  - Prop. 1.4: torsion coefficients are 0 or 1. The normal form itself is stated just before Prop. 1.4 and in Sec. 2.1; eventual coefficients equal to 1 come from Prop. 2.2.
  - Sec. 2.1: tau ~ Delta/(1-t) when H_1 = Z.
  - Cor. 2.3, first clause: boundary-incompressible and Floer simple implies norm = deg bar-Delta - 1, with no irreducibility needed.
- I re-derived the alternation argument: Delta''(1) = 2 sum (-1)^{k-j} n_j^2 > 0 unless Delta = 1.
- With Delta = 1, Cor. 2.3 would give norm -1, so dM compresses. Step 2's irreducibility then makes M a solid torus.
- Irreducibility cannot be dropped: (S^1 x D^2) # (Poincare sphere) is Floer simple with H_1 = Z and bar-Delta = 1.
- RR's remark in Sec. 1.1, that the H_1 = Z case with empty D^tau is boundary compressible, corroborates the conclusion.
- Needed: RF9, RF10.

**Step 4: holds, minor fixes.**
- M(lambda) = S^1 x S^2 comes from the actual unlink closure.
- I checked RR Prop. 7.8 (a knot in Z#(S^1 x S^2) with an L-space surgery has a generalized-solid-torus complement). It applies with Z = S^3 and L-space surgery M(alpha_2).
- Def. 7.2 gives deg bar-Delta < g_M = 1. RR's printed defining relation for g_Y is garbled, but each stated equivalent, and also |T| = k_Y g_Y, gives g_M = 1. The torsion formula in RR's proof gives bar-Delta ~ 1 directly.
- Torsion-free H_1 and irreducibility rule out the known generalized solid tori that are not solid tori.
- A shorter route is available: Sikora Prop. 10(1) (CJM Prop. 2.1(1)) gives a unique two-string solution for the unlink closure.
- Needed: RF11.

**Step 5 and coverage: holds, minor fixes.**
- The case split is exhaustive, and probes with unknot closures are covered.
- Y = S^3 and "Y is an L-space" are never assumed.
- Every filling is identified through an actual homeomorphism. Determinants are used only for the orders of homology groups.
- Cor. 20 is applied only to rational tangles, so Thm 24(c), which is equivalent to the Jones conjecture, is correctly avoided.
- One sentence is needed to pass from Lickorish's pair-homeomorphism rationality to a marked framed rational tangle (RF12).

**Counterexample search: none found.** Each candidate construction either violates a hypothesis or is excluded by a correctly applied result:
- Sikora's unframed pair <inf>, <-1/2>.
- Moving framing between the two arcs. Balanced isotopy absorbs this. Under ordinary framed isotopy rel boundary it would give a counterexample, so the convention matters, and the manuscript states it correctly.
- Orientation-reversed lens surgeries.
- Dual knots.
- Reducible Floer simple exteriors.
- Generalized solid tori with torsion.
- Berge exteriors.

The unframed analogue appears to fail (unknot and T(2,5) closures). This confirms that the framed hypothesis does real work, and it enters exactly in Step 2.

## 3. Required changes

- **RF1.** Scope of Thm 21. Restrict X to two-band framed tangles, or note that the proof of Thm 21 applies verbatim when closed components are present.
- **RF2.** State that the bracket is a balanced-isotopy invariant, so the closure brackets are exactly equal and [X] = [R] holds in Z[A^{+-1}]^2.
- **RF3.** Write out the closure expansion [N(X+T)] = [X]_0[N(<0>+T)] + [X]_inf[N(<inf>+T)], using the same framed closing tangle for X and R. Cite det(L) = |[L](e^{i pi/4})|.
- **RF4.** Stoimenow Prop. 6.5 states only that det is odd iff L is a knot. Cite it for that, and add the journal data.
- **RF5.** Replace [D, Sec. 3] with a proof that H_1 of the double branched cover is presented by a matrix of determinant +-det. This gives finite order det when det != 0 and infinite H_1 when det = 0 (e.g. Lickorish, GTM 175, Ch. 9).
- **RF6.** Write out the irreducibility case split: if M = M' # N, then N = S^3, or M'(alpha) = S^3 and N = M(alpha) is a homology sphere, hence S^3. Then: prime with boundary implies irreducible.
- **RF7.** Write out the orientation argument: balanced isotopy is ambient isotopy; dM and dV carry the same lifted orientation; the lifts are the identity or -I. So the signed coefficients in (1) agree.
- **RF8.** Cite Boyer-Lines Thm 2.8 as the primary source and Ni-Wu as a restatement. Restrict the claim to integral homology spheres, fix the normalization, and note that other normalizations do not affect the subtraction.
- **RF9.** Credit the torsion normal form to the paragraph before RR Prop. 1.4, Sec. 2.1 and Prop. 2.2. Justify D = +t^h Delta_K from D(1) = 1 = Delta_K(1). Define deg.
- **RF10.** Point back to Step 2 for irreducibility and justify the solid-torus lemma.
- **RF11.** Change "shared product" to "shared closure link". In Prop. 7.8, set Z = S^3 and name the L-space surgery and the homological longitude. Also derive g_M = 1 from |T| = k_M g_M.
- **RF12.** Add Conway's classification (BM Thm 3.6) and the Alexander trick before applying Cor. 20.
- **RF13.** References:
  - CJM numbering for [S]: Prop. 1 = 1.1, Cor. 19 = 7.1, Cor. 20 = 7.2, Thm 21 = 8.1, Prop. 10 = 2.1.
  - [BM]: the arXiv title says "applications". Add the published version, MPCPS 150(3) (2011) 505-525.
  - Add Lickorish (1981), Boyer-Lines, and arXiv:1009.4720.
  - Add journal data for [St] and [D].
- **RF14.** Cite Gainullin inside Step 3, at the Casson-Walker comparison and at the Delta'' sign argument. List the exact differences from his Thm 8.2:
  - the comparison is with L(p,q), not Y#L(p,q);
  - the second slope removes lambda_CW(Y);
  - Floer simplicity of the exterior replaces the L-space hypothesis on Y;
  - RR Cor. 2.3 plus irreducibility replaces genus detection.

Full wording for each fix is given in the required_fixes field.

## 4. Optional improvements

- State the two-slope lemma separately: a knot in an integral homology sphere with two orientation-preserving matched unknot surgeries is the unknot in S^3.
- Add a remark isolating where framing enters: only through Thm 21, which supplies determinants 0 and 1, and Cor. 20. Record the resulting unframed corollary.
- Cross-check Step 4 against Sikora Prop. 10(1).
- Credit Ozsvath-Szabo, KMOS and Ni.
- Remove internal workflow language from the front matter.

## 5. Novelty and attribution

Two independent sweeps found no prior proof. The conjecture's author presented it as open on 15 Oct 2026. The ingredients are all published. What is new:
- the observation that Thm 21 fixes the homological peripheral structure of the cover;
- a two-slope Casson-Walker plus Floer-simple characterization of the solid torus.

The second item is Gainullin's Thm 8.2 and KMOS method used in a new setting, not a corollary of either. The novelty is plausible but the priority is unverified, because of search coverage gaps and possible concurrent work by Sikora (based on talk captions). The modest framing should be kept.

## 6. Open issues

- Priority.
- No outside specialist review yet.
- Some classical sources were checked only through restatements: Boyer-Lines, Walker, Lickorish 1981, and Lickorish's textbook.
- RR Prop. 7.8's general-case proof is brief. It is avoidable through Sikora Prop. 10(1), whose proof was not audited.
- The content of the IPAM talk is known only from auto-captions.

## 7. Recommendation

Valid with minor revisions. After RF1-RF14 are applied, the argument is a complete and correctly attributed deduction of Sikora's Conjecture 2 from published results. Before posting, I recommend a specialist read and a priority check with the conjecture's author.
